PageBlocks.Title: Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter – key facts 1
PageBlocks.Content:
Key facts

All movements are in seasonally adjusted chain-volume terms (adjusted for price inflation) unless otherwise stated.

In the June 2026 quarter, compared with the March 2026 quarter:

  • GDP rose 0.2 percent
  • expenditure on GDP rose 0.4 percent
  • GDP per capita rose 0.1 percent
  • real gross national disposable income fell 0.4 percent.

The following movements are in seasonally adjusted nominal terms (not adjusted for price inflation).

In the June 2026 quarter, compared with the March 2026 quarter:

  • expenditure on GDP rose 0.5 percent
  • income GDP rose 0.6 percent.

New Zealand economy up in June 2026 quarter

Economic activity rose 0.2 percent in the June 2026 quarter as measured by gross domestic product. This follows a 0.9 percent rise in the March 2026 quarter. GDP rose 1.7 percent over the year ended June 2026, compared with the year ended June 2025.

Expenditure on GDP rose 0.4 percent in the June 2026 quarter, following a 1.1 percent rise in the March 2026 quarter. Expenditure on GDP rose 2.2 percent over the year ended June 2026, compared with the year ended June 2025.

PageBlocks.Title: Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter – key facts 4
PageBlocks.Content:
Upwards drivers – change in production

Construction was up 2.7 percent, driven by:

  • construction services
  • residential building construction.

Public administration and safety was up 2.0 percent, driven by:

  • central government administration and justice.

Health care and social assistance was up 0.8 percent, driven by:

  • central government health care and social assistance
  • private sector residential care services and social assistance.

Wholesale trade was up 1.3 percent, driven by:

  • machinery and equipment wholesaling
  • other goods wholesaling.

Downwards drivers – change in production

Transport, postal, and warehousing was down 1.7 percent, driven by:

  • road transport
  • transport support services.

Retail trade and accommodation was down 1.0 percent, driven by:

  • accommodation
  • food and beverage services.

PageBlocks.Title: Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter – key facts 5
PageBlocks.Content:
Upwards drivers – change in expenditure

Exports of goods and services was up 3.3 percent, driven by:

  • meat products
  • other food, beverages, and tobacco
  • dairy products.

Gross fixed capital formation was up 1.5 percent, driven by:

  • residential buildings
  • intangible fixed assets
  • plant, machinery, and equipment.

Imports of goods and services was down 0.8 percent (a fall in imports has an upwards contribution to expenditure on GDP), driven by:

  • travel services
  • imports of intermediate goods.

Downwards drivers – change in expenditure

Change in inventories decreased by $289 million, driven by:

  • distribution
  • manufacturing.

Central government final consumption expenditure was down 2.0 percent, driven by:

  • intermediate consumption plus taxes on production
  • social benefits in kind
  • an increase in sales (an increase in sales has a downwards contribution to the overall movement).

New Zealand’s real purchasing power falls in the June 2026 quarter

In the June 2026 quarter, compared with the March 2026 quarter:

  • real gross national disposable income fell 0.4 percent
  • real gross national disposable income per capita fell 0.6 percent.

In the year ended June 2026, compared with the year ended June 2025:

  • annual real gross national disposable income rose 2.5 percent
  • annual real gross national disposable income per capita rose 1.9 percent.

While GDP measures economic activity, real gross national disposable income (RGNDI) measures the volumes of goods and services that New Zealand residents have command over, that is, the real purchasing power of the country’s disposable income. RGNDI is also affected by changes in the terms of trade, the country’s net investment income, and net transfer flows with the rest of the world.

New Zealand’s ability to buy goods and services from its income, RGNDI, fell 0.4 percent in the June 2026 quarter. Net transfer flows increased, terms of trade decreased, and net investment income on our international investments increased.

Over the June 2026 quarter, export prices rose 3.5 percent, while import prices rose 13.8 percent, resulting in a decrease in the terms of trade. A decrease in the terms of trade results in more exports being needed to pay for a given volume of imports. This means that residents can purchase fewer goods and services by volume from the income generated from a given level of domestic production.

The 0.4 percent decrease in RGNDI, coupled with a population increase of 0.2 percent over the quarter, decreased RGNDI per capita by 0.6 percent in the quarter.

Annually, RGNDI rose 2.5 percent over the year to June 2026 while RGNDI per capita rose 1.9 percent over the year.

Quarterly nominal expenditure GDP, June 2026 quarter

The following movements are in seasonally adjusted nominal terms (not adjusted for price inflation) unless otherwise stated.

Seasonally adjusted nominal expenditure GDP rose 0.5 percent in the June 2026 quarter. The size of the economy was $455 billion for the year ended June 2026.

Nominal income GDP rises

Nominal income GDP rose 0.6 percent in the June 2026 quarter, following a 1.8 percent rise in the March 2026 quarter. The drivers were:

  • compensation of employees, up 1.0 percent
  • taxes on production and imports, up 1.2 percent.

PageBlocks.Title: Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter – key facts 6
PageBlocks.Content:
Impact of conflict in the Middle East on GDP in the June 2026 quarter

The measures of GDP in the June 2026 quarter were impacted by the Middle East conflict and related fuel price increases. Our headline measure of GDP is presented in volume terms, which removes the effect of price changes. However, GDP for some industries related to fuel saw changes which could be attributed to the large increases in fuel prices during the quarter.

In retail trade and accommodation, fuel retailing fell in volume terms in the June 2026 quarter and was the largest quarterly decline since the COVID-19-affected September 2021 quarter.

Accommodation and food services fell 3.8 percent in the June 2026 quarter, indicating a potential change in discretionary spending.

In household consumption expenditure (HCE), the restaurants and hotels group fell in the June 2026 quarter, indicating a similar change in discretionary spending to that seen in the accommodation and food services sub-industry on the production side.

Transport, postal, and warehousing fell 1.7 percent in the June 2026 quarter, driven by a decline in road transport. The quarterly method for this sub-industry has used diesel delivery volumes since the March 2022 quarter.

The transport group of HCE fell 1.6 percent in the June 2026 quarter. The petrol and other vehicle fuels and lubricants components of non-durable goods HCE also fell during the June 2026 quarter.

Imports of refined petroleum in constant prices rose 5.3 percent in the June 2026 quarter compared with the March 2026 quarter, but rose 63.8 percent in current prices over the same period.

Imports of intermediate goods, processed fuels and lubricants (which includes diesel) in constant prices rose 19.8 percent in the June 2026 quarter compared with the March 2026 quarter, but rose 123.8 percent in current prices over the same period.

Increases in quarterly prices for petrol imports were the highest since December 1990, while increases for processed fuels and lubricants were the highest on record (data from September 1990).

We made no methodological changes to quarterly GDP in response to the Middle East conflict and elevated fuel prices.
